This feature corrects lens distortion and helps with fisheye cameras by removing warping. It supports calibration, remapping, and provides performance details like working in real-time and with multiple streams. Typical parameters include center, coefficients, and zoom. GDC in HiSilicon ISPs refers to the Geometric Distortion Correction (sometimes called “GDC” or “WDR/GDC block” in HiSilicon docs). It’s a hardware block in the ISP that corrects geometric lens distortions and performs image remapping/warping for wide-angle and fisheye lenses and for dewarping/panoramic stitching.

Key points / typical features
- Purpose: remove barrel/pincushion and fisheye distortion; perform dewarp and rectification so images look geometrically correct or produce rectilinear views from ultra-wide lenses.
- Input/output: works as part of the ISP pipeline, taking raw or pre-processed frames and outputting remapped frames for downstream encoding/display.
- Correction method: uses a lens model + calibration parameters (distortion coefficients, center, scale, radius) or precomputed mapping tables (LUTs) to remap pixels.
- Interpolation: hardware performs interpolation (typically bilinear; some implementations may support higher-order interpolation) when mapping non-integer source coordinates.
- Performance: hardware-accelerated so it can run in real time at the ISP’s supported resolutions and frame rates; may support multiple streams or different output resolutions (chipset-dependent).
- Controls exposed: enable/disable, lens model parameters (k1, k2, etc. or table upload), center/zoom/rotation, strength/scale, ROI and stride settings.
- Use cases: fisheye dewarp (surveillance panoramic cameras), wide-angle correction, digital PTZ on rectified output, stitching pre-processing.
- Limitations: degree of correction and visual quality depend on calibration accuracy and interpolation; extreme corrections can reduce sharpness or introduce artifacts; precise capabilities (max resolution, number of streams, available interpolation modes, table size) vary by HiSilicon SoC/firmware.

If you need specifics (registers, API calls, or exact capabilities), tell me which HiSilicon chipset or SDK/ISP version you’re using (e.g., HiSilicon Hi3516/Hi3559/HiSilicon ISP SDK version) and I can pull up the detailed parameters and register/API information.
